prompt: An L-shape is made of two rectangles: $4 \times 3$ and $2 \times 5$. What is the total area?
hint: An L-shape is hard to measure all at once. It becomes easy when you treat it as two rectangles joined together.

hints.text: An L-shape is hard to measure all at once. It becomes easy when you treat it as two rectangles joined together.
Find each rectangle's area: $4 \times 3$ for the first and $2 \times 5$ for the second. Then add the two areas.
$12 + 10 = 22$, so the total area of the L-shape is $22$ square units.

explanation: Split the L-shape into the two rectangles it is made of, because rectangle areas are easy to find.
The first rectangle has an area of $4 \times 3 = 12$ square units.
The second rectangle has an area of $2 \times 5 = 10$ square units.
The pieces do not overlap, so add them: $12 + 10 = 22$ square units in total.
